content:
I noticed that only one road map has been declared complete, so I looked into the situation with OrthogonalL2Bases.
In fact it has been complete since July 30. This was not clear without a build and detailed study. There was history and evaluation in STATUS.md which notes that the road map was largely completed, but its author/generator declined to judge section A2 saying "that work predates the material surveyed here, so its exact state is not established by this snapshot", and the file does not give any certificate one can check.
I checked the completion by writing and building a file Discharged.lean which restates each target from Suggested.lean and proves it using the TauCeti declaration which realizes it. This is needed because sometimes the name in TauCeti is slightly different from the original suggestion.
This file builds against the TauCeti commit recorded in the file, but note that subsequent changes can break it. In the example at hand there were two such name changes, made for good reasons. That is why the commit is recorded.
This is not the only check needed as the road map can have other requirements. I studied it more and the project looks good: I declare this roadmap complete.

I think Discharged.lean or something like it would be a helpful tool. One needs to decide if it is a frozen artifact (pinned to the original TauCeti commit) or should be updated with TauCeti. If the road map is frozen then the first option seems better and that is what I did in the following PR's. But it could be discussed.

In any case there is a need for a close out protocol.

I made a PR TauCetiRoadmap#232 which adds Discharged.lean. Once it lands I'll open a second PR to freeze it and move the roadmap to Completed. They have to go in sequence rather than as a stack, for a reason worth flagging separately.
I first opened these as a stack, then the review bot merged the second PR into the first within minutes with no approving review and no CODEOWNERS gate, even though it touched .github/. The protections appear to assume a PR targets main.

More details here.
Let's just edit Suggested.lean, rather than adding a new file. And move to Completed at the same time.

I redid it as a single PR TauCetiRoadmap#236. There is a small problem. The file lands under Completed/, outside the TauCetiRoadmap.* glob, so CI never builds the discharged version. I've verified it locally and it elaborates clean, but nothing in the PR proves it.
Good point! I have pushed further changes to TauCetiRoadmap#236, that ensure that we actually build everything in Completed/. I'll merge shortly.
